title: In an abstract Setoid-flavored ring, double negation is equivalent to the identity
statement: For any AlgS.Ring record R (an abstract carrier, a caller-supplied equivalence relation equiv with congruence fields for add/mul/neg, additive commutative group and distributive laws stated over equiv rather than Eq) and any a of R's carrier, equiv (neg (neg a)) a -- the additive-group cancellation chain zero -> add zero (neg(neg a)) -> add (add a (neg a)) (neg(neg a)) -> add a (add (neg a) (neg(neg a))) -> add a zero -> a, built entirely from negAdd/addComm/addAssoc/addCongr/addZero and the record's own equivTrans/equivSymm values (no kernel Eq.rec transport is available for a defined equivalence relation).

formal.statement: theorem AlgS.neg_neg : ((x0 : AlgS.Ring) -> ((x1 : AlgS.Ring.carrier x0) -> AlgS.Ring.equiv x0 (AlgS.Ring.neg x0 (AlgS.Ring.neg x0 x1)) x1))

evidence.supports: AlgS.neg_neg admits through the trusted kernel gate and type-checks fully applied at a genuinely free `a`, both instantiated at CReal.commRingS's AlgS.CommRing.toRingS projection and at AlgS.Ring.ofAlg(Int.ring) (concrete at the respective zero element and symbolic, closed via lam_over). Neither CReal nor Int has a named `neg_neg` kernel theorem to `def_eq`-compare against (grepped: CReal has none in CRealPrelude/creal/*.rs; Int's `int_prelude/gcd.rs::neg_neg` is a private, never-declared Rust proof-term helper), so this is a well-typedness measurement, not a def_eq match.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(RUST_MIN_STACK=1073741824 cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib --release -- neg_neg_instantiated_at_int_through_ofalg_concrete_and_symbolic generic_neg_neg_instantiated_at_creal_matches_creal_neg_neg_type --test-threads=1 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 2 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pinned pattern requires BOTH counts ('2 passed; 0 failed') across both instantiation-site tests.

notes: The Setoid-flavored analogue of Alg.neg_neg (ADR-1584), which is a direct instantiation of Alg.groupInvUnique in the Eq-flavored spine; AlgS has no equivalent InvUnique theorem, so this is proved directly by the additive-group chain rather than by instantiating a more general lemma.
